newsitem.title: USA: Oriente exports seen down by 24,000 bpd in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Oriente exports seen down by 24,000 bpd in Sept.

text.p: Exports of Ecuadoran Oriente crude oil are scheduled to drop by 24,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September to an average of about 215,000 bpd, a source at Ecuadoran state oil company Petroecuador said on Monday.
Two term contracts of 12,000 bpd each held by Oil-tex Petroleum and Commercial Oil Services are due to expire at the end of August, the source said.
This volume is slated to be absorbed by the local Esmeraldas refinery, which was recently expanded by 20,000 bpd to 110,000 bpd capacity.
"We're now finishing the interconnection of the units and the refinery should be running in one and half to two weeks," the source said.
The decline translates into two fewer export cargoes per month. The number of loadings planned for September is 14, compared to 16 cargoes in August.
The source said that three or four other term contracts are set to expire in October, potentially opening up some 45,000 bpd of Oriente crude for new customers.
The Esmeraldas refinery is located 200 miles (320 km) northwest of Quito.
Plans are underway to increase capacity on the trans-Ecuadoran pipeline to free up pent up production.
